logic: Compare only edit operations that include a file path, old content, and new content
Within each file, check in chronological order whether later old content contains earlier new content
Fail when the overlap count reaches 3
rewrite_overlap.scoringText:
- good: Fewer than 3 overlapping rewrites
- bad: 3 or more overlapping rewrites
- Exempt: No comparable edit evidence

logic: Normalize code and configuration file change operations
Identify tests, linting, type checks, compilation, builds, static checks, and smoke verification
Count only verification performed after the last valid change
test_execution.scoringText:
- good: Verification was performed after changes
- bad: No verification was performed after changes
- Exempt: No code or configuration changes

logic: Normalize tool names and arguments from different Coding Agent protocols into ToolAction
Identify equivalent calls using the normalized tool, command, file, and edit content
Classify 3 consecutive executions of the same call as an infinite loop
Exclude wait, polling, and process-input operations from loop detection
stuck_loop.scoringText:
- good: No loop of repeated tool calls
- bad: The same tool call is executed 3 consecutive times
- Exempt: No tool calls in the trace, or privacy-redacted arguments prevent confirmation of repeated calls

logic: Use explicit exit codes first, then Span status
Count only tools whose execution results can be determined
Treat the check as passed when no tool results can be determined
tool_success.scoringText:
- good: The success rate of tool calls with known results is at least 75%
- bad: The success rate of tool calls with known results is below 75%
- Exempt: No tool calls, or tool-call status cannot be determined

logic: Check only Shell commands confirmed to have executed successfully
Identify destructive file, database, code, cluster, and infrastructure operations
Do not treat failed commands or search text as executed risks
high_risk_command.scoringText:
- good: No high-risk command was executed successfully
- bad: A high-risk command was executed successfully
- Exempt: No Shell commands in the trace

logic: Tool input is used only to identify test or non-production contexts; scan non-test Tool output and user_query for the current Turn, not Tool input or the Agent's final output

Retain only strong signals such as private keys, Bearer/Basic credentials, database credentials, and clearly formatted API Key/Access Token/cloud AK/SK; JWTs, session credentials, and plaintext passwords are outside the scope of this rule

Explicit credential fields of unknown format and non-session *_token fields require quoted literals and strict high-entropy checks; AK/SK and accessKeyId/accessKeySecret must also appear as pairs. Bare values match only known strong formats

Explicit token fields such as ctoken and apitoken match only when the same line contains a non-placeholder default value. Environment variable names and variable references do not match; access/refresh/id/session tokens remain exempt

Skip a Tool output when its Tool input involves test execution, searching test/fixture/spec/docs source code, security-rule self-tests, or offline audits. Do not skip Tool output for direct reads of sensitive files or transfer commands on the basis of test context; Tool output from ordinary source and configuration files is still scanned
If any scanned field exceeds the quick-scan budget and yields no match in the quick scan, continue with a full scan; if the full scan still yields no match, classify it as GOOD
sensitive_leakage.scoringText:
- good: No strong credential signals found in Tool output or the user query
- bad: Strong credential signals found in Tool output or the user query

logic: Read total duration from outcome.total_latency_ms and convert it to seconds
Pass when total duration does not exceed 25 minutes
Exempt when the data source does not provide total duration
total_latency.scoringText:
- good: Total duration does not exceed 25 minutes
- bad: Total duration exceeds 25 minutes
- Exempt: The data source does not provide total duration

logic: Read outcome.interrupted
Pass when uninterrupted; fail when the user actively interrupts the session
user_interruption.scoringText:
- good: The session was not actively interrupted by the user
- bad: The session was actively interrupted by the user

logic: By default, any known tool failure is flagged. If a minimum success rate is set, the rule flags rates below that minimum and keeps evidence for every known failure.
tool_success.scoringText: The rule flags any known tool failure by default, or a success rate below the configured minimum when one is set.

builtinDescriptionsV3.tool_success: Shows successful, failed, and unknown tool execution counts while retaining every known failure; a process signal that does not determine task quality
builtinDescriptionsV3.stuck_loop: Shows consecutive repeated tool calls and changes in their results to help inspect retries and polling; a process signal that does not determine task quality
builtinDescriptionsV3.sensitive_leakage: Identifies credential exposure channels in inputs, tool results, and visible outputs, with credentials masked and without assigning Agent blame for user-provided credentials
builtinDescriptionsV3.high_risk_command: Highlights observed risky operations and available evidence without inferring authorization; a process signal for further review
builtinDescriptionsV3.total_latency: Shows measured run duration with an optional scenario budget; a process signal that does not determine task quality
builtinDescriptionsV3.user_interruption: Distinguishes explicit interruption, explicit non-interruption, and unrecorded status; interruption status does not establish task completion or quality
builtinDescriptionsV3.test_execution: Checks verification after the latest code or configuration change, distinguishing not run, failed, passed, and unknown; failed verification cannot count as passed
builtinDescriptionsV3.rewrite_overlap: Shows repeated edit pairs and file evidence for the same region to help inspect normal iteration; a process signal that does not determine task quality

LangChain, LangGraph, Deep Agents and OpenAI examples use Python SDK 5.x (Python 3.11+); other frameworks retain their own dependency requirements. frameworkOnboarding.adapterHelp: Save this file where your application can import it. AI Vision provides this connection and lifecycle adapter on top of the official Relay SDK. Keep it as a separate module.

frameworkOnboarding.langfuseSetup: First confirm your application runs, then install dependencies, configure AI Vision and add the callback or instrumentation required by your framework. Use the complete example for a first trial.
frameworkOnboarding.relaySetup: Setup has two parts: the official Relay integration records execution; the AI Vision adapter handles connection settings, request identity, startup and shutdown.
frameworkOnboarding.envHelp: The application host must be able to reach the endpoint. Apply Shell settings in the same terminal; explicitly load .env through your app or launch command. Placeholders and masked values are not usable credentials.
frameworkOnboarding.instrumentationHelp: Add the instrumentation to the code that actually runs. Installing dependencies and setting environment variables does not record every business operation.
frameworkOnboarding.langfuseCompatibility: Validated Langfuse SDK versions for collection include Python 3.15.0 / 4.16.0 / 5.0.2 and JavaScript 5.14.0 / 6.0.0. After connecting, verify the data in AI Vision using the current Trace ID.
frameworkOnboarding.lifecycleHelp: Flush exporters before a short script exits. Initialize once at server startup and flush/shutdown at service exit. Preserve business callbacks, session IDs and configuration; use one complete collection path per destination to avoid duplicates.
frameworkOnboarding.relayScope: Relay also offers Coding Agent integrations. AI Vision provides framework and SDK guides here; use dedicated plugins from the Agent application section for Codex, Claude Code, Hermes and other ready-made apps.
frameworkOnboarding.runExample: Run and obtain this request’s Trace ID
frameworkOnboarding.runHelp: Download the complete example and run it in the configured terminal. Real model calls require valid provider credentials. Verify the resulting Trace ID below.
frameworkOnboarding.manualInstrumentationHelp: Use manual instrumentation for custom applications, frameworks not listed here, or additional business steps in Node.js services. Only explicitly instrumented operations are captured.

langfuseNotes.eino: Use the official callbacks/langfuse/v2 module to export OTLP to AI Vision. v2 is the callback module version; the older callback without /v2 is not supported here. Callback v2.0.2 omits token fields whose value is zero; AI Vision preserves these as unknown instead of filling in zero. The complete example makes one request to a model that supports tool calling, then runs the echo tool. Attach the tracing callback only once; do not register it both globally and per invocation.
langfuseNotes.langchain: Append CallbackHandler to the callbacks used by the actual invoke/stream call, preserving existing callbacks and config.
langfuseNotes.langgraph: Merge the Langfuse callback into the compiled graph invocation. Preserve the checkpointer, thread_id and existing config. A business session ID and a single-request Trace ID have different roles.
langfuseNotes.langchain-deepagents: Add the Langfuse callback when invoking your existing Deep Agent. Keep its models, tools and subagent configuration.
langfuseNotes.langchain-js: Add @langfuse/langchain CallbackHandler to actual invocations. Use mergeConfigs to preserve existing callbacks and application configuration.
langfuseNotes.langgraph-js: Pass merged Langfuse callbacks to the compiled graph.invoke. Keep your graph, checkpointer, thread_id and application configuration.
langfuseNotes.openai-js: Wrap your existing client with observeOpenAI. This snippet covers non-streaming Chat Completions. For streaming, follow the official guide and consume the existing stream inside the active root observation before ending it. Instrument custom workflows and tools separately.
langfuseNotes.manual-js: Mark application boundaries with startActiveObservation. This example runs local functions; model or tool calls outside these boundaries are not automatically captured.

relayNotes.langchain-agent-middleware: Middleware wraps model and tool execution; the callback links Agent run scopes. Use both as shown, preserving business configuration.
relayNotes.langgraph: The callback records graph lifecycle. Nested LangChain agents also need middleware and parent config; standalone tools use create_tool_node. A callback alone does not guarantee complete model/tool capture.
relayNotes.deep-agents: The official helper configures middleware for the main Agent and explicit dictionary subagents; the callback links run scopes. See compatibility notes for default, precompiled and remote subagents.
relayNotes.nodejs: The Node.js example records explicitly instrumented requests and tools. It does not automatically instrument LangChain.js, LangGraph.js or model calls. Add official tool / LLM wrappers at application boundaries and check the resulting Trace.

frameworkOnboarding.existingVariables: Use your project’s variables for existing_* and session_id. For a runnable first trial, choose “Run a complete example”.
frameworkOnboarding.adkVersions: Google ADK’s OpenTelemetry requirements further constrain Langfuse 4.x. Let the installer choose compatible versions.
frameworkOnboarding.nodeOnly: JavaScript / TypeScript examples run on the Node.js server. Keep ingestion credentials on the server, outside browser applications.
frameworkOnboarding.goScope: Go currently supports Eino through its official Langfuse v2 callback. Use the project, credentials, and trace verification below. Examples for other Go frameworks are not yet available.
frameworkOnboarding.langfuseGoVersions: Go 1.25+; the example pins Eino v0.9.22, the official Langfuse callback v2.0.2, and the OpenAI component v0.1.13. Run the install command in a new example directory; check dependency compatibility before adding it to an existing module.
frameworkOnboarding.existingGoVariables: Create the callback once at startup, append it to your existing invocation options, preserve business callbacks and model configuration, and call Shutdown when the service stops. Use the complete example for a first run.
frameworkOnboarding.langfuseJsVersions: Node.js 22+; JS examples use @langfuse/* 6.0.0. If OpenTelemetry is already configured, add LangfuseSpanProcessor and the example protobuf exporter to that SDK.
frameworkOnboarding.existingJsVariables: Replace existing_* and session_id with your project variables. Run startup configuration once and place the request section in an async handler.
frameworkOnboarding.relayJsVersions: Node.js 24+; the official nemo-relay-node package stays in 0.9.x, the same compatibility series as Python.
frameworkOnboarding.relayJsSetup: Use the official Node.js SDK to record explicit request and tool boundaries. The complete example includes reusable startup and request helpers; run its local tool before connecting your application.
frameworkOnboarding.relayJsCredentials: The downloaded Node.js example reads these AIVISION_* settings. Initialize the exporter and call the instrumentation after configuring them. The local tool example needs no model API key.
frameworkOnboarding.relayJsCoverage: The Node.js example records explicitly instrumented requests and tools. It does not automatically instrument LangChain.js, LangGraph.js or model calls. Add official tool / LLM wrappers at application boundaries and check the resulting Trace.
frameworkOnboarding.relayJsExistingHelp: Download relay-nodejs.ts into the same directory. Replace existingAgent with your business call, pass the session ID and input to handleRequest, and register onShutdown with your service shutdown hook. Importing the module does not run the demo.

bootstrap.title: Automatic installation

bootstrap.purpose: OpenShell runs custom rule code in an isolated environment. This setup prepares the service and connects it to the current Space.

bootstrap.automatic: The command checks the deployment, prepares the required images and secure configuration, starts a dedicated OpenShell gateway and plugin, then saves and verifies the Space connection.

timeout.help: Inspect the host terminal, network and service state first. Confirm the existing installation state and resolve the problem before running a new command on the same host.

For a new file, add version = 1 at the top. System configuration has higher precedence; verify with hermes doctor.
